"AQUARIA: FISHING WORLDS ONLINE

A 2D Multiplayer Fishing Sandbox MMORPG

PROJECT TYPE: 2D Side-View Pixel-Art Sandbox MMORPG
PLATFORM: Android Mobile + Desktop Web
ART DIRECTION: Modern Detailed Pixel Art (16-bit / 32-bit inspired)
TARGET PERFORMANCE: 60 FPS
MULTIPLAYER TARGET: 10–15 real players per world/room
MAIN GAMEPLAY: Fishing, Exploration, Habitat Building, Crafting and Social Multiplayer.

1. GAME VISION

Create an original, beautiful and fully playable 2D fishing sandbox MMORPG named AQUARIA.

AQUARIA is a living online world where players can fish, explore, collect rare fish, build their own environments, create custom aquatic habitats, craft equipment, trade with other players and develop their own fishing identity.

Fishing must be the main activity, but players must also have complete freedom to build and customize their own worlds.

The game must feel like a real persistent sandbox MMORPG, not a simple fishing simulator or a static prototype.

IMPORTANT:
Use the attached concept art as visual direction. Do not reproduce the poster as a single game screen. Build the actual game, separate game assets, UI, environments and gameplay systems.

Create original characters, environments, creatures, item designs and world structures.

2. WORLD AND CHARACTER DESIGN

Create a 2D side-view tile-based world.

Character features:

- Customizable character appearance.
- Multiple hairstyles.
- Different outfits.
- Hats and accessories.
- Fishing animations.
- Walking and running animations.
- Jumping and falling animations.
- Idle animations.
- Rod casting and reeling animations.
- Different fishing poses.

Movement:

- Walk left and right.
- Jump.
- Climb ladders.
- Stand on platforms.
- Interact with objects.
- Enter different environments.

World features:

- Forests.
- Lakes.
- Rivers.
- Waterfalls.
- Beaches.
- Oceans.
- Caves.
- Mountains.
- Snow environments.
- Tropical islands.
- Hidden fishing locations.

Create a seamless and expandable tile-based world.

3. BUILDING AND BLOCK SYSTEM

Players must be able to construct their own worlds.

Implement:

- Grid-based block placement.
- Block removal.
- Block inventory.
- Block stacking.
- Building mode.
- World saving.
- Personal building areas.

Block categories:

NATURAL BLOCKS:
Grass, dirt, stone, sand, mud, snow, ice, clay and crystal.

BUILDING BLOCKS:
Wood, stone bricks, glass, metal, decorative tiles and platforms.

AQUATIC BLOCKS:
Water blocks, deep-water blocks, freshwater blocks and special biome water blocks.

DECORATIVE BLOCKS:
Corals, aquatic plants, glowing crystals, seaweed, flowers, lanterns and underwater decorations.

INTERACTIVE OBJECTS:
Doors, chests, signs, ladders, workbenches, fishing stations, aquarium tanks and display stands.

Water blocks are extremely important.

Players must be able to place water blocks to construct their own ponds, lakes, rivers, swimming pools and fishing environments.

The water system should support different depths and visual appearances.

4. ADVANCED FISHING MECHANICS

Fishing is the core gameplay system.

Implement a complete fishing process:

1. Equip a fishing rod.
2. Select bait or lure.
3. Stand near suitable water.
4. Cast the fishing line.
5. Wait for a fish to bite.
6. Display a visual bite indicator.
7. Start a fishing timing minigame.
8. Control tension while reeling.
9. Successfully catch the fish.
10. Display fish name, rarity, weight and value.
11. Automatically add the fish to inventory.

Fishing must be interactive.

Include:

- Casting distance.
- Reel speed.
- Fishing tension.
- Line durability.
- Fish resistance.
- Fish escape probability.
- Bite timing.
- Different fish behaviours.

Large fish should be harder to catch.

Rare fish should require better equipment, suitable bait or special environmental conditions.

5. FISHING RODS

Create a large fishing rod progression system.

Rod types:

1. Beginner Rod.
2. Wooden Rod.
3. Fiberglass Rod.
4. Carbon Rod.
5. Professional Rod.
6. Deep Sea Rod.
7. Golden Rod.
8. Crystal Rod.
9. Ancient Rod.
10. Legendary Rod.
11. Mythical Rod.

Every rod must have its own appearance and statistics.

Rod statistics:

- Casting Distance.
- Reel Speed.
- Line Strength.
- Fish Control.
- Luck.
- Rarity Bonus.
- Durability.

Some rods should specialize in certain fishing environments.

Examples:

- Deep Sea Rod: better deep-water performance.
- Crystal Rod: special bonuses in crystal habitats.
- Golden Rod: improved general fishing statistics.
- Ancient Rod: special bonuses against ancient fish.

Create unique visual effects for rare and high-tier rods.

6. REELS, LINES AND HOOKS

Fishing equipment must be customizable.

Reel categories:

- Basic Reel.
- Bronze Reel.
- Steel Reel.
- Advanced Reel.
- Precision Reel.
- Deep Sea Reel.
- Legendary Reel.

Fishing line categories:

- Basic Line.
- Nylon Line.
- Fluorocarbon Line.
- Braided Line.
- Reinforced Line.
- Deep Sea Line.
- Mythical Line.

Hook categories:

- Small Hook.
- Medium Hook.
- Large Hook.
- Barbed Hook.
- Heavy Hook.
- Special Hook.

Different equipment must affect fish-catching performance.

For example, a stronger line should help catch heavy fish, while a precision reel should improve tension control.

7. LURES AND BAIT

Create a detailed bait and lure collection.

LURES:

- Spinner.
- Spoon.
- Minnow.
- Frog.
- Crankbait.
- Soft Plastic.
- Glow Lure.
- Crystal Lure.
- Deep Sea Lure.
- Electric Lure.
- Legendary Lure.
- Mythical Lure.

NATURAL BAIT:

- Worms.
- Grubs.
- Insects.
- Small Minnows.
- Shrimp.
- Crustaceans.
- Special Bait.

Different species must prefer different bait and lures.

Examples:

- Worms attract common freshwater fish.
- Minnows attract predatory fish.
- Glow Lures work better at night.
- Shrimp attracts certain tropical and coastal fish.
- Deep Sea Lures attract ocean species.
- Special Lures unlock rare fishing opportunities.

Lures should have different effectiveness, durability and rarity.

8. ACCESSORIES AND BUFF SYSTEM

Create a comprehensive equipment and accessory system.

Equipment slots:

- Headgear.
- Necklace.
- Gloves.
- Ring.
- Boots.
- Backpack.
- Special Charm.

Examples:

Lucky Necklace:
Increases rare fish probability.

Angler Hat:
Increases fishing experience.

Precision Gloves:
Improves fishing control.

Golden Ring:
Provides additional luck.

Deep Sea Charm:
Improves deep-water fishing.

Treasure Compass:
Increases treasure discovery chances.

Explorer Boots:
Improves movement speed.

Fishing Backpack:
Increases inventory capacity.

Crystal Pendant:
Improves fishing in crystal habitats.

Accessories must have different rarity levels:

Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary and Mythical.

Allow players to combine equipment bonuses.

Prevent unlimited stacking and maintain balanced gameplay.

9. FISH COLLECTION AND RARITY

Create a large and expandable fish database.

Rarity categories:

- Common.
- Uncommon.
- Rare.
- Epic.
- Legendary.
- Mythical.
- Secret.

Every fish must have:

- Unique sprite.
- Name.
- Description.
- Rarity.
- Weight range.
- Selling price.
- Preferred biome.
- Preferred depth.
- Preferred bait.
- Preferred time.
- Catch probability.

EXAMPLE FISH COLLECTION:

COMMON:
Bluegill, River Minnow, Small Carp, Catfish, Silver Perch.

UNCOMMON:
Rainbow Trout, Red Snapper, Yellowfin, Mudfish.

RARE:
Golden Koi, Electric Eel, Crystal Perch, Emerald Pike.

EPIC:
Shadow Bass, Frostfin, Phantom Ray, Thunder Eel.

LEGENDARY:
Ancient Dragonfish, Golden Leviathan, Phantom Marlin.

MYTHICAL:
Celestial Whale, Abyssal Serpent, Eternal Koi.

SECRET:
Create hidden fish species with extremely rare discovery conditions.

Fish must have randomized weights within their species-specific weight ranges.

A 2 kg fish and a 20 kg fish of the same species should not necessarily have the same selling price.

Add personal records and fish collection achievements.

10. CUSTOM AQUATIC HABITATS

THIS IS ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT FEATURES OF AQUARIA.

Players must be able to create their own fishing habitats using water blocks and environmental blocks.

Build a habitat recognition system that detects:

- Water volume.
- Water depth.
- Block composition.
- Nearby vegetation.
- Special decorations.
- Environmental conditions.

BIOME EXAMPLES:

FRESHWATER POND:
Water + Dirt + Grass.

TROPICAL HABITAT:
Water + Sand + Coral + Tropical Plants.

DEEP OCEAN:
Large water volume + sufficient depth.

FROZEN LAKE:
Water + Ice + Snow.

SWAMP:
Water + Mud + Swamp Vegetation.

CRYSTAL HABITAT:
Water + Crystal Blocks + Glowing Decorations.

VOLCANIC HABITAT:
Water + Volcanic Rocks + Special Decorations.

MAGICAL HABITAT:
Water + Rare Crystals + Special Biome Objects.

Players must be able to build these habitats in different shapes and sizes.

Do not limit players to predefined lakes or rivers.

FISH SPAWNING RULES:

- Tropical fish require tropical habitats.
- Deep sea fish require sufficient depth.
- Frozen fish prefer frozen environments.
- Swamp fish prefer muddy environments.
- Crystal fish require special environmental conditions.
- Secret fish require special block combinations or discovery conditions.

Create a Habitat Information Panel displaying:

- Habitat Type.
- Water Depth.
- Habitat Quality.
- Fish Species Available.
- Environmental Requirements.
- Rare Fish Conditions.

Allow players to discover new habitat combinations.

11. UNDERWATER ENVIRONMENT

Create beautiful underwater visual environments.

Features:

- Animated water.
- Underwater lighting.
- Bubbles.
- Aquatic plants.
- Coral reefs.
- Rocks.
- Underwater caves.
- Swimming fish.
- Rare underwater treasures.

Fish should move naturally within suitable water areas.

Different fish should have different movement patterns and swimming speeds.

12. CRAFTING AND ECONOMY

Implement a functional crafting system.

Crafting stations:

- Workbench.
- Fishing Equipment Table.
- Bait Station.
- Reel Workshop.
- Aquarium.
- Fish Display Station.

Players can craft:

- Fishing rods.
- Reels.
- Fishing lines.
- Hooks.
- Lures.
- Bait.
- Accessories.
- Building blocks.
- Decorative objects.

Economy:

- Sell fish.
- Buy equipment.
- Trade items.
- Purchase bait.
- Upgrade equipment.
- Earn coins through quests.
- Open player shops.

Create a balanced in-game currency system.

13. MULTIPLAYER MMORPG

REAL MULTIPLAYER IS A CORE REQUIREMENT.

Target 10–15 real players per shared world or room.

Features:

- Player accounts.
- Unique usernames.
- Real-time player movement.
- Player appearance synchronization.
- Shared environments.
- Player chat.
- Friends system.
- Private messages if supported.
- Fishing together.
- Trading.
- Player shops.
- Visiting player habitats.
- Fishing competitions.
- Leaderboards.

Players must be able to see each other moving, jumping and fishing in real time.

Do not simulate multiplayer using NPCs or duplicated local characters.

Use a real networking backend and server-authoritative state if supported.

Save player data and world changes persistently.

If the platform cannot support real multiplayer directly, explain the exact missing backend or networking requirements and build the game with a multiplayer-ready architecture.

Do not falsely claim that multiplayer is functional if it is only simulated.

14. PROGRESSION AND SKILLS

Create a player leveling system.

Player progression categories:

- Fishing Level.
- Building Level.
- Exploration Level.
- Crafting Level.

Players gain experience through:

- Catching fish.
- Discovering new species.
- Completing fishing challenges.
- Exploring new biomes.
- Building habitats.
- Crafting equipment.

Higher levels unlock:

- Better fishing rods.
- New lures.
- Special accessories.
- New fish species.
- New crafting recipes.
- New environments.
- Advanced building blocks.

Create achievements and milestones.

15. INVENTORY AND FISH JOURNAL

Build a fully functional inventory.

Inventory categories:

- Fish.
- Rods.
- Reels.
- Lines.
- Hooks.
- Lures.
- Bait.
- Accessories.
- Blocks.
- Materials.
- Consumables.
- Quest Items.

Features:

- Item stacking.
- Item sorting.
- Item descriptions.
- Equipment slots.
- Rarity indicators.
- Item statistics.
- Sell and trade functions.

FISH JOURNAL:

Create a fish collection book.

Show:

- Discovered species.
- Undiscovered fish silhouettes.
- Fish descriptions.
- Rarity.
- Weight records.
- Preferred habitat.
- Preferred bait.
- Personal catch records.

16. QUESTS AND EVENTS

Add fishing quests and exploration missions.

Examples:

- Catch 10 common fish.
- Catch a fish above 10 kg.
- Discover a new biome.
- Build a tropical habitat.
- Catch a legendary fish.
- Help another player.
- Find a secret fish.

Add limited-time fishing competitions and seasonal events.

17. DAY/NIGHT AND WEATHER SYSTEM

Create:

- Sunrise.
- Daytime.
- Sunset.
- Nighttime.
- Rain.
- Fog.
- Snow.
- Storms.

Fish availability should change depending on time and weather.

Some fish only appear:

- During nighttime.
- During rain.
- At sunrise.
- During storms.
- Under special environmental conditions.

18. PETS AND COSMETICS

Allow players to collect cosmetic pets and companions.

Examples:

- Small Turtle.
- Blue Fish Companion.
- Floating Jellyfish.
- Baby Dragonfish.
- Crystal Crab.

Pets may provide small cosmetic or utility bonuses, but must not overpower fishing equipment.

Add outfits, hairstyles, fishing animations and character customization.

19. USER INTERFACE AND CONTROLS

Create a polished, responsive mobile-friendly UI.

Main interface:

- Player Profile.
- Health or character status if needed.
- Currency.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Fish Journal.
- Crafting.
- Habitat Information.
- Map.
- Quests.
- Shop.
- Friends.
- Chat.
- Settings.

MOBILE CONTROLS:

- Virtual movement joystick.
- Jump button.
- Interact button.
- Cast Fishing button.
- Reel button.
- Inventory button.
- Building Mode button.

DESKTOP CONTROLS:

- Keyboard movement.
- Jump controls.
- Mouse interaction.
- Keyboard shortcuts.

Make all UI elements functional.

Avoid controls covering the main gameplay area.

20. VISUAL ART DIRECTION

Use the attached AQUARIA concept artwork as the main visual reference.

Create an original modern detailed pixel-art aesthetic.

Visual requirements:

- Medium-sized detailed pixel art.
- 16-bit/32-bit-inspired style.
- Smooth character animations.
- Beautiful turquoise and deep blue water.
- Detailed vegetation.
- Rich natural environments.
- Unique fish silhouettes.
- Beautiful equipment sprites.
- Distinctive biome designs.
- Atmospheric lighting.
- Attractive underwater effects.

Do not use excessively tiny pixels.

Do not create blurry or low-resolution-looking assets.

Do not copy existing game characters, logos, maps, UI or proprietary assets.

Maintain visual consistency across all environments and items.

21. PERFORMANCE AND TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

Target 60 FPS.

Optimize for Android mobile devices and desktop browsers.

Requirements:

- Efficient tile rendering.
- Optimized character movement.
- Lightweight animations.
- Responsive UI.
- Efficient multiplayer synchronization.
- Persistent data storage.
- Modular architecture.
- Reusable game components.

Keep game data organized in structured JSON or equivalent data definitions where possible.

Separate:

- Fish database.
- Rod database.
- Lure database.
- Accessory database.
- Block database.
- Biome rules.
- Crafting recipes.
- Player statistics.

Make it easy to add new fish, equipment, habitats and content without rebuilding the entire game.

22. ADMIN AND DEBUG SYSTEM

If supported, create an administrator system.

Authorized administrators can:

- Spawn fish.
- Add items.
- Adjust rarity.
- Modify fish weights.
- Modify fishing probabilities.
- Edit equipment statistics.
- Create new species.
- Inspect player information.
- Manage world data.

Protect administrator access with proper authorization.

23. DEVELOPMENT ORDER

Do not attempt to generate every feature simultaneously if doing so reduces quality.

Build the game in stages.

STAGE 1 — CORE PLAYABLE GAME:

- Character movement.
- World generation.
- Tile-based building.
- Water blocks.
- Basic fishing.
- 10 initial fish species.
- Basic fishing rods.
- Inventory.
- Saving and loading.

STAGE 2 — ADVANCED FISHING:

- Multiple rods.
- Reels.
- Lines.
- Hooks.
- Lures.
- Bait.
- Accessories.
- Buffs.
- Fish rarity.
- Fish weight.
- Fishing Journal.

STAGE 3 — HABITAT SYSTEM:

- Custom water environments.
- Biome detection.
- Water depth.
- Habitat quality.
- Fish spawning rules.
- Secret fish conditions.

STAGE 4 — MULTIPLAYER:

- Player accounts.
- Real-time movement.
- Shared worlds.
- Chat.
- Trading.
- Friends.
- Persistent multiplayer data.
- 10–15 player target.

STAGE 5 — EXPANSION:

- More fish.
- More biomes.
- More blocks.
- Advanced crafting.
- Quests.
- Events.
- Pets.
- Leaderboards.
- Special discoveries.

24. FIRST BUILD INSTRUCTIONS

START BUILDING NOW.

Do not simply explain how the game could be created.

Generate the actual playable Stage 1 game.

Prioritize:

1. A beautiful playable 2D pixel-art environment.
2. Functional player movement.
3. Functional water block placement and removal.
4. Functional fishing mechanics.
5. Functional fish catching.
6. Inventory and fish collection.
7. Persistent player progress.

After the first build, test all important interactions.

Do not create decorative buttons that do nothing.

If a feature is not supported, explain the limitation and continue implementing the working features.

FINAL VISION

AQUARIA must become a living, expandable online fishing sandbox MMORPG.

Every player should be able to develop their own fishing style, build unique aquatic habitats, discover rare fish, collect powerful equipment, explore beautiful environments and interact with other players.

The world should encourage creativity, exploration, competition and social interaction.

FISH MORE. BUILD BETTER. EXPLORE DEEPER. BECOME A LEGEND.

WELCOME TO AQUARIA — FISHING WORLDS ONLINE.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Stage 1 of “AQUARIA: FISHING WORLDS ONLINE,” a 2D side-view pixel-art fishing sandbox MMORPG.
- Deliver a polished browser game with movement, fishing, building, inventory, saving, and clear multiplayer limitations.

## Requirements
- Create original modern detailed pixel-art presentation and a separate game environment/UI, not a poster.
- Implement Stage 1 gameplay: character movement, tile world, water placement/removal, fishing, 10 fish species, basic rods, inventory, and persistent progress.
- Make all controls functional; do not add decorative nonfunctional buttons.
- Keep the game mobile-friendly and suitable for desktop.
- Real multiplayer should not be falsely represented as implemented.

## Decisions
- Implemented the first build as a single-player, local-save browser game.
- Used original canvas-rendered pixel-art visuals and a persistent local storage save system.
- Marked multiplayer as requiring an account service, authoritative game server, and persistent multiplayer database.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the complete main game shell and responsive UI.
- Added animated pixel-art cove environment, player character, camera, terrain, water, reeds, plants, clouds, and lighting.
- Added left/right movement, jumping, canvas interaction, touch controls, and keyboard controls.
- Added building mode, block selection, block placement/removal, and block inventory.
- Added custom water blocks and persistent world edits.
- Added casting, bite timing, tension/reeling minigame, randomized weighted catches, rarity, coins, and fish capture modal.
- Added 10 initial fish species in the fish database logic.
- Added inventory, selling fish, fish journal, habitat scanner, map, quests, crafting, and settings panels.
- Added automatic local saving for coins, catches, records, inventory, blocks, world edits, and player position.
- Added a local HTTP server on port 3002 for browser testing.

### Active
- No active implementation work remains in this conversation.

### Blocked
- Real multiplayer is unavailable in the current architecture and is explicitly documented as a backend-dependent feature.
- No real player accounts, shared rooms, chat, trading, friends, leaderboards, or server-authoritative persistence were implemented.

## Next Move
1. Add the missing real multiplayer backend and account system if Stage 4 is to be implemented.
2. Browser-test and refine fishing, building, and mobile touch interactions.
3. Expand beyond Stage 1 with additional rods, reels, lines, hooks, bait, habitats, quests, and pet/cosmetic systems.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/AQUARIA/AQUARIA/index.html`: Main game markup and UI structure.
- `/home/runner/work/AQUARIA/AQUARIA/style.css`: Full visual styling and responsive/mobile layout.
- `/home/runner/work/AQUARIA/AQUARIA/game.js`: Game logic, rendering, saving, fishing, building, and modal systems.

## Important Context
- Stage 1 is implemented as a locally persistent browser game; there are no simulated multiplayer players.
- Progress is stored in browser `localStorage` under key `aquaria-stage1-v1`.
- The game can be served locally with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Untracked/changed project files include `index.html`, `style.css`, `game.js`, `README.md`, `Agents.md`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, `capture.sh`, and existing environment files.
